html:
The Mutapa Empire was a Shona state on the northern Zimbabwean Plateau, between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers. The map shows it from 1492 to 1600. Its name comes from the royal title Mwene we Mutapa, "lord of the conquered lands", which the Portuguese wrote as Monomotapa.

Tradition says it was founded in the 1400s by Nyatsimba Mutota, a prince from the south, as Great Zimbabwe declined. Its wealth was gold, mined on the plateau, and ivory, sold to Swahili merchants who carried them to the coast at Sofala and into the trade of the Swahili city-states.

From the early 1500s the Portuguese pushed up the Zambezi to Sena and Tete to reach the gold. A Portuguese army sent against Mutapa around 1570 was destroyed by disease and fighting. But succession wars weakened the kingdom, and in 1629 a Mutapa ruler signed a treaty that made him a Portuguese vassal and opened the land to traders and settlers of Portuguese East Africa.

In the 1680s and 1690s the Rozvi under Changamire Dombo drove the Portuguese off the plateau and took over the south. A smaller Mutapa state survived in the Zambezi valley into the 1800s.
